description: List the release policies that evaluate every publish of an organization, and the checkers it can configure: Valet's own, and the organization's, which set_checker adds. An organization checker shows its URL, its headers (a credential header shows only its references), the release files it was approved to receive, and why it is unavailable or what its last call got wrong. Each policy shows its checker, its enforcement (monitor, or block at a severity), its settings, and how its evaluations came out over the last 30 days. A secret setting shows as (set), never its value. Call it before publishing to see what will be evaluated, and fix what you can first. A blocking policy refuses a release with a finding at or above its severity; a monitor policy reports and never refuses. Requires connecting a Valet account.

org_name.description: The Valet organization whose release policies to list. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

name: list_policies

checkers.description: The checkers a policy can run: Valet's own and the organization's.

described_at.description: When Valet last tried to describe an organization checker endpoint, as an RFC 3339 time, whether or not it worked. Absent for a Valet checker.

display_name.description: The name a person reads. Empty when the checker declares none.

fields.description: The settings a policy can give this checker.

description.description: What the setting is for. Empty when the checker gives none.

name.description: The setting's name, which set_policy takes as a key of settings.

required.description: True when a policy must give this setting.

secret.description: True when a person enters the value on a request page, not in settings.

headers.description: An organization checker's headers, by name. A credential header shows only its {{NAME}} references and scheme word. Absent when there are none.

inputs.description: The release files an organization checker was approved to receive: source, build, or both. Absent when it asked for none.

last_error.description: What the organization checker's last call got wrong, with credentials redacted as [redacted]. Absent when nothing is recorded.

name.description: The checker's name as a policy spells it, such as catalog:secrets or org:snyk.

origin.description: Who provides the checker: valet for Valet's own, organization for one the organization added with set_checker.

unavailable.description: Why a policy cannot use the checker now. Absent when it can.

url.description: An organization checker's base URL. Absent for a Valet checker, or when the stored checkers could not be read.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

policies.description: The organization's release policies. Empty when it has none, so no publish is evaluated.

applies_to.description: Which releases the policy evaluates. every_release means every publish.

block_at.description: The lowest severity that blocks: info, low, medium, high, or critical. Absent for a monitor policy.

checker.description: The checker the policy runs, spelled as set_policy takes it, such as catalog:secrets or org:snyk.

enforcement.description: monitor records findings and never refuses a release. block refuses a release with a finding at or above block_at.

name.description: The policy's name, which destroy_policy takes.

read_only.description: True for installation policies; only a Valet administrator can change them.

recent.description: How this policy's evaluations came out over the last 30 days.

at_or_above.description: Evaluations that found a finding at or above each severity, keyed by info, low, medium, high, and critical.

errored.description: Evaluations that could not run to a decision.

evaluations.description: Evaluations of releases in the last 30 days.

last_error.description: Why the latest errored evaluation could not run, with credentials redacted as [redacted]. Empty when none errored.

passed.description: Evaluations that let the release go ahead.

scope.description: installation or org; installation policies apply to every org.

settings.description: The policy's checker settings, by field name. A secret field shows (set), never its value.

redactions.description: How many credentials were replaced with [redacted] in the text this answer was built from: secret values the service holds, and strings shaped like an API key, a private key, a token, or a password in a URL or header. Redaction is best effort, so 0 does not prove the text holds no credential.

title: List release policies
